reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, with the same two orders and amounts. Next I'll list the orders so I can check that the refunds line up with the order records before paying anyone.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, and both refunded orders exist with refund amounts below their order totals. Nothing suggests the refund work is incomplete or wrong, so I'll proceed to get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 48125 matches my check: orders 210 (31647) and 213 (31611) total 63258, less the 15133 refund on order 213, gives 48125. Next I'll get birch's balance.
Birch's balance of 67298 matches my check: orders 211 (38685) and 214 (35281) total 73966, less the 6668 refund on order 214, gives 67298. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its balance next.
Cobalt's balance of 46961 matches orders 212 (32516) and 215 (14445), with no refunds. All three balances check out against the ledger, so I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch and cobalt still need payouts; their balances already matched my independent check against the orders and refunds, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt is the last customer, and its balance of 46961 matches orders 212 and 215 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers have been paid, and each balance matched my independent check against the orders and refunds. The task is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
